# NepDate - Complete API Reference

Version: 2.1.0 | License: MIT | NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages/NepDate/ | GitHub: https://github.com/RajuPrasai/NepDate

Targets: netstandard2.0 and net8.0. Every name below exists in the public API; anything not listed here does not exist.

---

## Getting Started

**Install:**
```
dotnet add package NepDate
```

**Quick start:**
```csharp
using NepDate;

// Today in BS
var today = NepaliDate.Today;
Console.WriteLine(today); // e.g. "2083/08/03"

// BS to AD
var bs = new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15);
DateTime ad = bs.EnglishDate; // 2023-10-02

// AD to BS
var bs2 = new NepaliDate(DateTime.Today);
var bs3 = DateTime.Today.ToNepaliDate(); // extension method
```

---

## NepaliDate struct

`namespace NepDate`
`readonly partial struct NepaliDate : IComparable, IComparable<NepaliDate>, IEquatable<NepaliDate>, IFormattable`
(net8.0 build also: `ISpanFormattable, IParsable<NepaliDate>, ISpanParsable<NepaliDate>`)

### Constructors and static members

```csharp
NepaliDate(int yearBs, int monthBs, int dayBs)
NepaliDate(DateTime engDate)                     // time part and DateTimeKind are ignored
NepaliDate(string rawNepaliDate)                 // "2080/06/15", "2080-6-15", ...
NepaliDate(string rawNepaliDate, bool autoAdjust, bool monthInMiddle = true)

static NepaliDate Today { get; }                 // local date
static NepaliDate Now { get; }                   // same date as Today
static readonly NepaliDate MinValue              // 1901/01/01 BS = 1844-04-11 AD
static readonly NepaliDate MaxValue              // 2199/12/30 BS = 2143-04-15 AD

static NepaliDate Parse(string rawNepaliDate)
static NepaliDate Parse(string rawNepaliDate, bool autoAdjust, bool monthInMiddle = true)
static bool TryParse(string rawNepDate, out NepaliDate result)
static bool TryParse(string rawNepDate, out NepaliDate result, bool autoAdjust, bool monthInMiddle = true)
```

### Properties

```csharp
int Year                  // BS year (1901-2199)
int Month                 // BS month (1-12)
int Day                   // BS day (1-32)
DateTime EnglishDate      // Gregorian date at midnight, DateTimeKind.Unspecified
DayOfWeek DayOfWeek       // System.DayOfWeek
NepaliMonths MonthName    // NepaliMonths.Ashoj for month 6
int MonthEndDay           // Days in this month (29, 30, 31 or 32)
int DayOfYear             // 1 on 1 Baisakh
bool IsDefault            // true for default(NepaliDate)

// Calendar data. See "Calendar Data" for the years covered; other dates return empty values.
string TithiNp            // Tithi in Devanagari, e.g. "दशमी*"; empty string when none
string TithiEn            // Tithi in English, e.g. "Dashami (K)"; empty string when none
bool IsPublicHoliday      // Nepal gazetted public holiday
string[] EventsNp         // Event names in Devanagari; empty array when none
string[] EventsEn         // Event names in English; empty array when none
```

### Methods

```csharp
NepaliDate AddDays(double days)
NepaliDate AddMonths(double months, bool awayFromMonthEnd = false) // false clamps to the month end
NepaliDate AddYears(int years, bool awayFromMonthEnd = false)
NepaliDate MonthEndDate()                     // last day of this month
TimeSpan Subtract(NepaliDate nepDateTo)       // same as left - right
bool IsLeapYear()                             // Gregorian leap year of EnglishDate
bool IsToday()
bool IsYesterday()
bool IsTomorrow()
CalendarInfo GetCalendarInfo()                // all calendar data in one lookup; prefer it in loops
void Deconstruct(out int year, out int month, out int day)   // var (y, m, d) = date;
int CompareTo(NepaliDate other)
bool Equals(NepaliDate other)

TimeSpan operator -(NepaliDate left, NepaliDate right)
bool operator ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=
```

```csharp
var d = new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15);
d.AddDays(20);                               // 2080/07/05
d.AddMonths(-2);                             // 2080/04/15
new NepaliDate(2081, 4, 32).AddMonths(1);    // 2081/05/31 (clamped)
new NepaliDate(2081, 4, 32).AddMonths(1, awayFromMonthEnd: true); // 2081/06/01
(d - new NepaliDate(2080, 1, 1)).Days;       // 171
```

### Fiscal year

Nepal's fiscal year runs from 1 Shrawan (month 4) to the last day of Ashad (month 3) of the next year.

```csharp
NepaliDate FiscalYearStartDate(int yearOffset = 0)
NepaliDate FiscalYearEndDate(int yearOffset = 0)
(NepaliDate startDate, NepaliDate endDate) FiscalYearStartAndEndDate(int yearOffset = 0)
NepaliDate FiscalYearQuarterStartDate(FiscalYearQuarters fiscalYearQuarters = FiscalYearQuarters.Current, int yearOffset = 0)
NepaliDate FiscalYearQuarterEndDate(FiscalYearQuarters fiscalYearQuarters = FiscalYearQuarters.Current, int yearOffset = 0)
(NepaliDate startDate, NepaliDate endDate) FiscalYearQuarterStartAndEndDate(FiscalYearQuarters fiscalYearQuarters = FiscalYearQuarters.Current, int yearOffset = 0)

static NepaliDate GetFiscalYearStartDate(int fiscalYear)
static NepaliDate GetFiscalYearEndDate(int fiscalYear)
static (NepaliDate startDate, NepaliDate endDate) GetFiscalYearStartAndEndDate(int fiscalYear)
static NepaliDate GetFiscalYearQuarterStartDate(int fiscalYear, int month)
static NepaliDate GetFiscalYearQuarterEndDate(int fiscalYear, int month)
static (NepaliDate startDate, NepaliDate endDate) GetFiscalYearQuarterStartAndEndDate(int fiscalYear, int month)
```

```csharp
var d = new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15);
d.FiscalYearStartDate();                       // 2080/04/01
d.FiscalYearEndDate();                         // 2081/03/31
d.FiscalYearQuarterStartAndEndDate();          // (2080/04/01, 2080/06/30)
NepaliDate.GetFiscalYearStartAndEndDate(2080); // (2080/04/01, 2081/03/31)
```

---

## Formatting

```csharp
string ToString()                                   // "2080/06/15"
string ToString(DateFormats dateFormat, Separators separator = Separators.ForwardSlash, bool leadingZeros = true)
string ToUnicodeString(DateFormats dateFormat = DateFormats.YearMonthDay, Separators separator = Separators.ForwardSlash, bool leadingZeros = true)
string ToLongDateString(bool leadingZeros = true, bool displayDayName = false, bool displayYear = true)
string ToLongDateUnicodeString(bool leadingZeros = true, bool displayDayName = false, bool displayYear = true)
string ToString(string format, IFormatProvider formatProvider = null)   // IFormattable
```

```csharp
var d = new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15);
d.ToString(DateFormats.DayMonthYear, Separators.Dash);       // "15-06-2080"
d.ToString(DateFormats.MonthDayYear, Separators.Dot, false); // "6.15.2080"
d.ToUnicodeString();                                         // "२०८०/०६/१५"
d.ToLongDateString();                                        // "Ashoj 15, 2080"
d.ToLongDateString(displayDayName: true);                    // "Monday, Ashoj 15, 2080"
d.ToLongDateUnicodeString(displayDayName: true);             // "सोमवार, असोज १५, २०८०"
d.ToString("D");                                             // "Ashoj 15, 2080"
d.ToString("s");                                             // "2080-06-15"
d.ToString("MMMM dd, yyyy");                                 // "Ashoj 15, 2080"
$"{d:yyyy-MM-dd}";                                           // "2080-06-15"
```

Standard formats: `null`, `""`, `"G"`, `"g"`, `"d"` give `yyyy/MM/dd`; `"D"` gives the long date; `"s"` gives `yyyy-MM-dd`.
Custom tokens: `yyyy`, `yy`, `MMMM` (month name), `MMM` (first 3 letters), `MM`, `M`, `dd`, `d`. Quote literal text with `'...'` or escape one character with `\`.

On net8.0, `ISpanFormattable.TryFormat` is an explicit interface implementation: `((ISpanFormattable)d).TryFormat(buffer, out int written, "s", null)`.

---

## Parsing

### Strict: NepaliDate.Parse / TryParse / constructor

Year, month and day in that order, ASCII digits, separated by `/`, `-`, `.`, `_`, `\`, space, `|` or `।`.

```csharp
NepaliDate.Parse("2080-06-15");                    // 2080/06/15
NepaliDate.Parse("2080/6/15");                     // 2080/06/15
NepaliDate.Parse("15-06-2080", autoAdjust: true);  // 2080/06/15
NepaliDate.TryParse("2080/13/01", out var bad);    // false
```

Strict parsing does not accept month names, Nepali digits or "20800615". Use SmartDateParser for those words and digits.

### Smart: SmartDateParser (static class, namespace NepDate)

```csharp
static NepaliDate Parse(string input)                    // FormatException when it cannot read the input
static bool TryParse(string input, out NepaliDate result)
// Extension methods on string: ToNepaliDate(), TryToNepaliDate(out NepaliDate)
```

```csharp
SmartDateParser.Parse("15 Ashoj 2080");      // 2080/06/15
SmartDateParser.Parse("Asoj 15, 2080");      // 2080/06/15
SmartDateParser.Parse("15th Shrawan 2080");  // 2080/04/15
SmartDateParser.Parse("२०८० असोज १५");        // 2080/06/15
SmartDateParser.Parse("२०८०/०६/१५");          // 2080/06/15
SmartDateParser.Parse("080/6/15");           // 2080/06/15
SmartDateParser.Parse("2080/04/15 BS");      // 2080/04/15
```

Accepted month spellings (sample):
- Baishakh: Baisakh, Baishakh, Vaishakh, Baisak
- Jestha: Jestha, Jeshtha, Jesth, Jeth
- Ashad: Ashadh, Ashad, Asad, Asar, Ashar
- Shrawan: Shrawan, Shravan, Sawan, Saun
- Bhadra: Bhadra, Bhadau, Bhado, Bhadon
- Ashoj: Ashoj, Ashwin, Aswin, Asoj
- Kartik: Kartik, Kartick, Karthik
- Mangsir: Mangsir, Mangshir, Margashirsha
- Poush: Poush, Push, Paush
- Magh: Magh, Maagh
- Falgun: Falgun, Phalgun, Phagun
- Chaitra: Chaitra, Chait

---

## NepaliDateRange

`namespace NepDate`
```csharp
readonly struct NepaliDateRange : IEnumerable<NepaliDate>, IEquatable<NepaliDateRange>

NepaliDateRange(NepaliDate start, NepaliDate end)
static NepaliDateRange SingleDay(NepaliDate date)
static NepaliDateRange FromDayCount(NepaliDate start, int days)
static NepaliDateRange ForMonth(int year, int month)
static NepaliDateRange ForFiscalYear(int fiscalYear)
static NepaliDateRange ForCalendarYear(int year)
static NepaliDateRange CurrentMonth()
static NepaliDateRange CurrentFiscalYear()
static NepaliDateRange CurrentCalendarYear()

NepaliDate Start { get; }
NepaliDate End   { get; }
bool IsEmpty     { get; }   // Start > End
int Length       { get; }   // days in the range, inclusive

bool Contains(NepaliDate date)
bool Contains(NepaliDateRange other)
bool Overlaps(NepaliDateRange other)
bool IsAdjacentTo(NepaliDateRange other)
NepaliDateRange Intersect(NepaliDateRange other)
NepaliDateRange Union(NepaliDateRange other)
NepaliDateRange[] Except(NepaliDateRange other)
NepaliDateRange[] SplitByMonth()
NepaliDateRange[] SplitByFiscalQuarter()
IEnumerable<NepaliDate> DatesWithInterval(int interval)
IEnumerable<NepaliDate> WorkingDays(bool excludeSunday = false)   // never includes Saturday
IEnumerable<NepaliDate> WeekendDays(bool includeSunday = true)
string ToString()                                                  // "2080/06/01 - 2080/06/30"
string ToString(DateFormats format, Separators separator = Separators.ForwardSlash)
```

**Example:**
```csharp
var ashoj = NepaliDateRange.ForMonth(2080, 6);
ashoj.Length;                                           // 30
ashoj.Contains(new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15));            // true
ashoj.IsAdjacentTo(NepaliDateRange.ForMonth(2080, 7));  // true
ashoj.Except(NepaliDateRange.FromDayCount(new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 10), 5));
// [2080/06/01 - 2080/06/09, 2080/06/15 - 2080/06/30]
foreach (var day in ashoj)
    Console.WriteLine(day);
```

---

## Bulk Conversion

`BulkConvert` is a public class nested in `NepaliDate`.

```csharp
IEnumerable<NepaliDate> NepaliDate.BulkConvert.ToNepaliDates(IEnumerable<DateTime> engDates, bool useParallel = true)
IEnumerable<DateTime>   NepaliDate.BulkConvert.ToEnglishDates(IEnumerable<NepaliDate> nepDates, bool useParallel = true)
IEnumerable<DateTime>   NepaliDate.BulkConvert.ToEnglishDates(IEnumerable<string> nepDates, bool useParallel = true)
IEnumerable<NepaliDate> NepaliDate.BulkConvert.BatchProcessToNepaliDates(IEnumerable<DateTime> engDates, int batchSize = 1000)
IEnumerable<DateTime>   NepaliDate.BulkConvert.BatchProcessToEnglishDates(IEnumerable<NepaliDate> nepDates, int batchSize = 1000)
```

Each call converts the whole collection in one pass on the calling thread, keeps the input order and returns a filled collection. An invalid date throws from the call itself. `useParallel` and `batchSize` are kept for source compatibility and do not change the result; `batchSize < 1` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

---

## Calendar Data

```csharp
using NepDate.Core.Calendar;

var d = new NepaliDate(2081, 6, 26);
CalendarInfo info = d.GetCalendarInfo();
// info.TithiNp         = "दशमी*"
// info.TithiEn         = "Dashami (K)"
// info.IsPublicHoliday = true
// info.EventsNp        = ["विजया दशमी", "देवी विसर्जन"]
// info.EventsEn        = ["Vijaya Dashami", "Devi Visarjan"]
```

Data bundled with the library:

| Data | Years covered |
|---|---|
| Tithi | 2078-2083 BS |
| Events and public holidays | 2077-2083 BS, plus a few days of 2084 BS |

Every other date returns empty strings, `false` and empty arrays. No exception is thrown.

---

## Serialization

Types are in `namespace NepDate.Serialization`.

### System.Text.Json

On the net8.0 build `NepaliDate` carries `[JsonConverter(typeof(SystemTextJsonConverters.NepaliDateJsonConverter))]`, so no configuration is needed:

```csharp
string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { Date = new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15) });
// {"Date":"2080-06-15"}
```

Object format, or the netstandard2.0 build (for example .NET Framework):

```csharp
var options = new JsonSerializerOptions().ConfigureForNepaliDate(useObjectFormat: true);
JsonSerializer.Serialize(new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15), options);
// {"Year":2080,"Month":6,"Day":15}
```

On netstandard2.0 your project must reference System.Text.Json 8.0.5 or later.

### Newtonsoft.Json

```csharp
var settings = new JsonSerializerSettings().ConfigureForNepaliDate();   // or useObjectFormat: true
string json = JsonConvert.SerializeObject(new { Date = new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15) }, settings);
// {"Date":"2080-06-15"}
// Converter classes: NewtonsoftJsonConverters.NepaliDateJsonConverter, NewtonsoftJsonConverters.NepaliDateObjectJsonConverter
```

Both `ConfigureForNepaliDate` overloads share a name, so a project calling either one must reference Newtonsoft.Json.

### XML

`NepaliDate` itself does not implement `IXmlSerializable`. Use the `NepaliDateXmlSerializer` wrapper:

```csharp
var serializer = new XmlSerializer(typeof(NepaliDateXmlSerializer));
using var writer = new StringWriter();
serializer.Serialize(writer, new NepaliDateXmlSerializer(new NepaliDate(2080, 6, 15)));
// <NepaliDateXmlSerializer>2080-06-15</NepaliDateXmlSerializer>
// Read back with ((NepaliDateXmlSerializer)serializer.Deserialize(reader)).Value
```

### ASP.NET Model Binding

`NepaliDate` has a registered `TypeConverter`, so it binds from route parameters, query strings and form fields:

```csharp
[HttpGet("{date}")]
public IActionResult GetRecord(NepaliDate date) { ... }
// Works for: /api/records/2080-6-15
// Also works for: ?date=2080-6-15
```

---

## Type System

### Interfaces implemented by NepaliDate

| Interface | Target | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `IComparable`, `IComparable<NepaliDate>` | both | Sorting and ordering |
| `IEquatable<NepaliDate>` | both | == and .Equals() |
| `IFormattable` | both | ToString(format, provider) |
| `ISpanFormattable` | net8.0 | Span formatting (explicit implementation) |
| `IParsable<NepaliDate>`, `ISpanParsable<NepaliDate>` | net8.0 | Generic parsing |

### TypeConverter

`NepaliDateTypeConverter` (namespace `NepDate.TypeConversion`) is registered via `[TypeConverter]`. It converts:
- `string` -> `NepaliDate` (strict parse)
- `int` -> `NepaliDate` (YYYYMMDD, e.g. 20800615)
- `DateTime` -> `NepaliDate`
- `NepaliDate` -> `string`, `int` or `DateTime`

---

## Enums

### NepaliMonths

```csharp
enum NepaliMonths
{
    Baishakh = 1,
    Jestha   = 2,
    Ashad    = 3,
    Shrawan  = 4,
    Bhadra   = 5,
    Ashoj    = 6,
    Kartik   = 7,
    Mangsir  = 8,
    Poush    = 9,
    Magh     = 10,
    Falgun   = 11,
    Chaitra  = 12
}
```

### DateFormats

```csharp
enum DateFormats { YearMonthDay, YearDayMonth, MonthYearDay, MonthDayYear, DayYearMonth, DayMonthYear }
```

### Separators

```csharp
enum Separators { ForwardSlash, BackwardSlash, Dot, Underscore, Dash, Space }
```

### FiscalYearQuarters

```csharp
enum FiscalYearQuarters
{
    Current = 0,   // the quarter of the date
    First   = 4,   // Shrawan-Ashoj (months 4-6)
    Second  = 7,   // Kartik-Poush (months 7-9)
    Third   = 10,  // Magh-Chaitra (months 10-12)
    Fourth  = 1    // Baishakh-Ashad (months 1-3)
}
```

---

## Exceptions

| Type | Namespace | Thrown when |
|---|---|---|
| `InvalidNepaliDateFormatException` (a `FormatException`) | NepDate | Text cannot be parsed, or a date-dependent member is used on `default(NepaliDate)` |
| `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` | System | Year, month or day out of range, or a result outside 1901-2199 BS |
| `ArgumentNullException` | System | A `BulkConvert` input collection is null, or `SmartDateParser.Parse` gets null or empty text |
| `FormatException` | System | `SmartDateParser.Parse` cannot read the input |

---

## Advanced

### Struct design

`NepaliDate` is an 8-byte `readonly partial struct`. Creating dates, converting and doing arithmetic allocate nothing on the heap.

### Thread safety

All instance and static members are thread-safe. The struct is immutable. `BulkConvert` converts on the calling thread and is safe to call from several threads.

### Dependencies

The package has no NuGet dependencies. Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json are referenced with `PrivateAssets=all`, so they are not added to your project. If you call the JSON helpers, reference the JSON library yourself (on the net8.0 build System.Text.Json comes with the runtime).

### Supported range detail

| BS | AD |
|---|---|
| 1901/01/01 BS | 1844-04-11 AD |
| 2199/12/30 BS | 2143-04-15 AD |

Calendar data covers fewer years: tithi 2078-2083 BS, events and holidays 2077-2083 BS. Other dates: TithiNp/TithiEn return empty strings, IsPublicHoliday returns false, EventsNp/EventsEn return empty arrays. No exception is thrown.
